en.title: Target Butt Numbering and Lane Positions
en.excerpt: Detailed explanation of archery range butt layout, lane numbering, wave shooting orders, and sub-target positions.
en.content:
Archery Range Target Numbering

Archery ranges are organized linearly with target butts numbered sequentially from left to right: Target 1, Target 2, Target 3... Target N. Each physical foam butt accommodates between two and four archers simultaneously.

Sub-Target Positions (A, B, C, D)

Every target butt is partitioned into four distinct athlete assignments:

  • Position A: Left archer shooting in Wave 1.
  • Position B: Right archer shooting in Wave 1.
  • Position C: Left archer shooting in Wave 2.
  • Position D: Right archer shooting in Wave 2.

Two-Wave Shooting Protocol (AB / CD)

In standard World Archery outdoor tournaments, archers alternate shooting order between ends:

  • End 1: Wave 1 (Archers A & B) shoots first, followed by Wave 2 (Archers C & D).
  • End 2: Wave 2 (Archers C & D) shoots first, followed by Wave 1 (Archers A & B).

Calculating Maximum Field Capacity

To determine range capacity: Total Foam Butts × 4 Athletes = Maximum Single-Session Capacity. For example, a range with 20 target butts accommodates 80 archers per qualification session.
